# Decision and Action Principles {.unnumbered}

Decision mechanisms matter only through the actions they select and the evidence they use to update the loop. This part treats tools, planners, and collaborators as components of one controlled execution graph rather than as independent features.

::: {#pri-typed-action .callout-principle title="Actions need explicit semantics"}

**Invariant**: Every action surface must define valid inputs, observable outputs, side effects, failure modes, and retry behavior.

**Implication**: Natural-language intent must be translated into a typed execution contract before it can safely cross the agent–environment boundary.

:::

::: {#pri-planning-value .callout-principle title="Planning must repay its overhead"}

**Invariant**: Additional search or deliberation is valuable only when its expected reduction in outcome loss exceeds its latency, compute, and coordination cost.

**Implication**: Systems should allocate test-time compute adaptively and preserve simple reactive paths when deeper planning adds little value.

:::

::: {#pri-coordination-boundary .callout-principle title="Decomposition creates interfaces"}

**Invariant**: Splitting work among agents introduces communication, consistency, and integration costs.

**Implication**: Multi-agent designs require explicit ownership and merge rules; additional agents do not create useful parallelism when the task remains tightly sequential.

:::
